questions.story: An employee receives a time-sensitive email containing a fake payment link and accidentally enters their business credentials on a spoofed portal.
questions.question: Which defensive control is most effective at preventing an attacker from using these stolen credentials to gain unauthorized entry?
options: Requiring complex passwords with special characters
Enforcing mandatory Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) via an authenticator app across all business accounts
Relying on web browser password auto-save features
questions.feedback: MFA provides a vital secondary barrier. Without physical access to the secondary token, stolen credentials alone cannot grant access.

questions.story: Attackers frequently create lookalike domain names to trick staff during payment confirmation requests.
questions.question: What technical protocol should your domain administrator configure to help external mail servers reject spoofed emails claiming to come from your official domain?
options: Changing the public display name on your email client
Implementing DMARC alongside SPF and DKIM authentication records
questions.feedback: DMARC/SPF/DKIM policies instruct receiving mail servers to automatically block or flag spoofed emails pretending to originate from your organization.

questions.story: An attacker attempts to log into your business account using credentials harvested from a phishing form.
questions.question: Which automated detection indicator alerts the business in real time that an unauthorized party is logging in?
options: Real-time automated alerts for unrecognized device logins, unfamiliar IP addresses, or impossible travel anomalies
Reviewing email login logs manually at the end of each billing cycle
Disabling administrative login notifications to avoid alert fatigue
Checking system CPU usage in Task Manager
questions.feedback: Instant push/SMS alerts for new devices or unexpected geographical logins allow immediate session revocation before damage occurs.

questions.story: After obtaining access to an account, an attacker silently alters account settings to maintain access without drawing attention.
questions.question: What specific configuration should be audited to detect hidden persistence mechanisms set up by an attacker?
options: Checking the total size of your inbox storage quota
Clearing your browser cache and cookies
Auditing account recovery details (phone numbers, secondary emails) and active API key connections
questions.feedback: Attackers frequently add shadow recovery addresses or authorized third-party applications to retain access after a password reset.
